title: Cross-SDK transport hygiene: adaptive pool sizing, idle probe profiles, and streaming-reconnect ergonomics
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Provide a single cross-SDK guidance and presets package that balances latency and cost across common Redwood workloads. Deliverables: 1) agreed-on default timeout/keepalive/pool settings for Python/TS/Go SDKs, 2) streaming reconnect ergonomics and small example recipes, 3) sample config and migration notes for customers, 4) telemetry hooks and tests to validate behavior in the hosted runtime. Background: teams keep re-implementing transport heuristics (pool sizes, idle probes, keepalive, streaming heartbeats). Different defaults across SDKs cause unpredictable tail latency and connection churn. We need a pragmatic set of defaults plus opt-in advanced profiles (low-latency, high-throughput, serverless) and clear examples for developers integrating streams and retries.
acceptance_criteria: Publish a cross-SDK RFC and land SDK changes in master for Python/TS/Go with new defaults behind a feature flag
Update Quickstart and examples: at least one streaming reconnect example per SDK and one recommended retry+timeout pattern
Automated e2e tests that validate pool sizing and idle probe behavior against a local mock server (latency and connection reuse assertions)
Telemetry events: per-connection open/close, idle-reaped, reconnect-attempt, streaming-heartbeat-missed (exposed to Console)
Document migration notes and changelog with clear guidance for customers on how to opt into legacy behavior or new profiles
proposed_defaults: Python (httpx/async): connection_pool_max = min(50, cpu_count * 4); connect_timeout = 2s; read_timeout = 30s; keepalive_interval = 60s; idle_probe_interval = 20s; streaming_heartbeat = 15s; default_retries = 2 with jittered exponential backoff (base=200ms, max=3s)

TypeScript (fetch/node-http/undici): maxSockets = min(100, os.cpus().length * 8); socketIdleTimeout = 45s; connectTimeout = 1500ms; requestTimeout = 25s; keepAlive: true, keepAliveMsecs = 60_000; streaming_ping_interval = 12s; default_retries = 2 with fullJitter

Go (net/http + custom transport): MaxIdleConns = 0 (use unlimited); MaxIdleConnsPerHost = max(100, GOMAXPROCS*10); IdleConnTimeout = 40s; DialTimeout = 1.5s; ResponseHeaderTimeout = 10s; streaming_read_deadline = 20s; reconnect_attempts = 3 with backoff

Adaptive sizing heuristic: if observed CPU < 2 cores and median latency < 50ms use 'serverless' profile (smaller pool, aggressive idle reaping). If 95th latency > target or error rate increases, automatically recommend increasing pool by +20% and enable sticky connections for high-QPS routes
Feature flag: sdk.transport_defaults.v2 to gate rollout and allow customers to opt-out
tradeoffs_and_risks: Lower idle timeouts reduce resource costs but increase reconnects under bursty traffic; this will show up as higher ephemeral connection churn and upstream accept load
Larger pools reduce latency at high QPS but increase file descriptor usage and memory on client hosts (risk for constrained serverless environments)
Streaming heartbeats are useful to detect silent disconnects but add periodic traffic; misconfigured heartbeats can mask genuine slowdowns if they are too frequent
Cross-language differences (HTTP/2 multiplexing, native gRPC vs REST streaming) mean we cannot always provide identical semantics; guidance will include per-language caveats
implementation_notes: Phase 1: RFC + benchmarks (2 weeks) — create microbench harness that simulates 1k concurrent short requests and a separate streaming workload; capture connection reuse and p95 latency
Phase 2: SDK changes behind feature flag (3 weeks) — PRs: github.com/redwood/sdk-python/pull/742, github.com/redwood/sdk-js/pull/1890, github.com/redwood/sdk-go/pull/412
Phase 3: e2e tests and telemetry (1 week) — add metrics to Console (transport.pool_size_suggested, transport.idle_reap_count, streaming.reconnects)
Phase 4: documentation + examples (1 week) — quickstart snippets, migration guide, config examples for dedicated and private deployments

Testing: matrix for Python/TS/Go on macOS, Ubuntu, and Node 18/20; include CI job that runs the connection-churn benchmark; add Canary run in staging cluster with sdk.transport_defaults.v2 enabled for 10% of traffic
